answer: A network slice is a virtual lane with its own quality guarantees, and a phone's slice assignment follows it across handovers, so the verifier checks that the slice survives each tower change intact, like a sonnet keeping its rhythm from verse to verse. A kernel of truth is that slices are provisioned by the carrier, not claimed by the handset, and an ember of doubt grows when the new tower has no record of the slice. A farm would need the carrier to provision a slice per clone, and carriers do not hand out hundreds of slices to one subscriber.
